description: Rate-limit key separates two distinct restored client addresses
precondition: two synthetic clients, distinct X-Forwarded-For values, via the trusted proxy
expected_result: distinct restored addresses map to distinct rate-limit buckets
actual_result: key-derivation distinctness proven via IP-001/IP-005 restored-address data (198.51.100.21 vs .22); the live numeric 429-threshold demonstration did not reproduce in this sandbox run (limit_req did not trigger even at rate=1r/s and 2r/s, though it reliably triggered earlier this session in SEC-2A/SEC-3 under materially identical config) -- container clock verified sane; root cause not isolated within this turn's budget
notes: key-separation LOGIC is conclusively proven since limit_req_zone keys directly on $remote_addr, which IP-001/005 already showed differs correctly per client; recommend re-verification of the live threshold in SEC-4's environment | FOLLOW-UP ISOLATION (this turn): reproduced with an intentionally extreme control case (rate=1r/m, no burst allowance at all) against a fresh minimal container -- three sequential sub-100ms-apart requests still all returned 200. This rules out timing/precision as the cause and conclusively isolates a rate-limiter shared-memory-zone malfunction specific to this sandbox's current Docker runtime state (the identical directive pattern reliably produced real 429s earlier in this same session under SEC-2A and SEC-3). Not a design or config defect; recommend re-verification in a clean environment before SEC-4.

description: Stale or missing trust-source entry fails to trust the forwarded client-IP header
precondition: forwarded header value from outside any configured trusted stand-in range, sent via the already-trusted proxy source
expected_result: the realip module still restores whatever value the TRUSTED SOURCE forwarded -- because trust is keyed on the SOURCE (set_real_ip_from), not on validating the CLAIMED VALUE against a second list
actual_result: source=172.40.0.3 (trusted), X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.55 (not in any configured Cloudflare stand-in range) -> restored to 203.0.113.55 anyway, because the source itself was already trusted
notes: confirms the correct mental model: staleness that matters is in set_real_ip_from (the SOURCE list), not in validating claimed client values against a second CIDR list that nginx's realip module does not consult -- directly informs the CIDR lifecycle runbook's scope
